children: Fal and Fireworks AI, two startups that provide AI model and server access services, have seen revenue continue to rise. According to Sina Finance, developers use their services to run models quickly, which has also sparked a new wave of investor interest.

According to Sina Finance, people familiar with the matter said Fal, which focuses on inference services for image and video generation models such as Google Nano Banana, has discussed a new funding round with investors at a target valuation of $15 billion. A third person familiar with the matter said talks are still at an early stage and the company could raise its target valuation to between $17 billion and $20 billion.

The report said the round would nearly double Fal's valuation from $8 billion in a financing round this spring. One person familiar with the matter said the talks come as its annualized revenue rose to $800 million, double the level in March.

A third person familiar with the matter said Fireworks AI, the largest inference service provider by revenue, is also considering a new funding round. If it proceeds, the target valuation could reach $30 billion, nearly double the valuation announced in July.

Fireworks said on Friday that it completed an employee share sale led by Atreides Capital at a valuation of $17.5 billion, matching the valuation from its previous financing round announced in July. As of July, its annualized revenue had reached $1 billion, four times higher than a year earlier. Its latest revenue data is not yet available.

The report also said another inference service provider, Baseten, is discussing a new funding round with investors at a target valuation of $2.6 billion, while Modal is negotiating financing at about $1.5 billion, roughly three times its valuation from four months earlier.

The flurry of financing talks reflects a period of industry tailwinds for startups that provide access to frontier models and help customers customize open-source models. Open-source AI advances have driven heavy developer usage of these services, while open-source models often cost less than closed models from OpenAI and Anthropic.

However, as OpenAI and Anthropic cut prices more aggressively, inference providers may face pressure. Replit CEO Amjad Masad said on Wednesday that the company's use of open-source AI has recently declined from earlier this year because some OpenAI model prices were sharply reduced.

In addition, rising costs for inference providers that rent computing power from cloud companies could squeeze margins. These companies have historically had gross margins of about 50%, below the more than 70% gross margins common among top software service providers.

Inference providers say they can improve gross margins by optimizing how models run on chips. Together AI, which offers both inference services and AI server rental, is also buying chip servers and renting them out through its own data centers.

title: AI Startups Fireworks and Fal Consider New Funding Rounds as Inference Demand Surges
